(b) For the year ended 31st March, 2026, Exceptional items represents income amounting to ₹ 1678.65 Lakhs include (i) ₹
580.49 lakhs on account of reduction in fixed, variable and Custody charges for the two Tejas express trains w.e.f. 1st April,
2024 to 31st March, 2025 in line with the letter received from Ministry of Railways and (ii) ₹ 1098.16 Lakhs being excess
provisions written back for previous years relating to various expenses. 
The figures for the previous year/periods have been regrouped/reclassified/restated, wherever considered necessary.
In line with Railway Board Commercial Circular No. CC-60 of 2019 on increase in catering tariff for post-paid and pre-paid trains,
the Company raised demands for enhanced licence fee for the periods 18th November 2019 to 22nd March 2020 (post-paid
trains) and 27th November 2021 to 30th September 2026 (post-paid and pre-paid trains). Certain licensees have challenged the
demands before High Courts or invoked arbitration. Awards passed against the Company in some cases have been challenged
before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court, which has stayed their execution; the matter is next listed on 18th January, 2027.
As the matter is sub-judice, the enhanced licence fee for the periods 18th November 2019 to 22nd March 2020 (post-paid
trains) and 27th November 2021 to 30th September 2026 (post-paid and pre-paid trains) has not been recognised in the results
for the quarter and half-year ended 30th September 2026, the corresponding comparative periods and the year ended 31 March
2026, consistent with earlier periods.
As per the terms and conditions of the tender, in respect of the four PPP Railneer plants, the Developer-cum-Operators (DCOs)
are to be reimbursed the GST on the supply of Railneer, net of the Input Tax Credit (ITC) availed by them. However, complete
information regarding the ITC availed by the DCOs is not available. Based on the information made available by certain DCOs, an
amount of ₹ 99.32 lakhs and ₹ 192.00 lakhs has been accounted for as a claim by the Company towards ITC for the quarter and
half year ended 30 September 2026, respectively, and an amount of ₹ 397.86 lakhs was accounted for during FY 2025-26.
Accordingly, the total amount accounted for in the books of the Company aggregates to ₹ 1847.30 lakhs and ₹ 2039.30 lakhs as
at 31 March 2026 and 30 September 2026, respectively. The DCOs have contested the Company's claim towards ITC. 
The management has issued letters to the DCOs directing them to furnish GSTR data, so as to enable IRCTC to ascertain the
actual ITC availed by them. Based on such data, recovery of ITC shall be affected strictly in accordance with the contract
conditions.
The DCOs of Sankrail, Hapur & Nagpur plants have challenged the same before the Hon’ble Court. In case of Sankrail Plant, the
Hon’ble Delhi High Court has appointed an Arbitrator and restrained the Company from taking any recovery related steps in
respect of any amount pertaining to the alleged input tax credit until the learned Sole Arbitrator takes up the application under
Section 17 for consideration. Similarly, in respect of Hapur and Nagpur plants, the matter are under arbitration before a
common Sole Arbitrator for these DCOs. In case of Parassala Plant, contract has been terminated and a notice of dispute has
already been issued. Necessary action will be taken in accordance with the concession agreement of Parassala Plant.
The National Anti-Profiteering Authority (NAA) had issued a notice dated 25 February, 2022 alleging profiteering of ₹5041.44
lakh under CGST Act, 2017 for on account of non-passing the benefit of tax reduction to consumers. The show cause notice was
contested by the Company; however, no order was passed by the Authority. Subsequently, Competition Commission of India
(CCI) was empowered to adjudicate the matter. The matter was taken up by the Principal bench of the Hon'ble Goods & Services 
Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT).
The Hon'ble GSTAT, vide its judgment dated 14 October 2026, has passed an order against the Company in relation to
proceedings under Section 171 of the CGST Act, 2017, concerning alleged profiteering in respect of Rail Neer packaged drinking
water. The Hon'ble Tribunal has accepted the DGAP report dated 11 June 2021 and directed the Company to deposit the alleged
profiteered amount of ₹5,041.44 lakh in the Central and State Consumer Welfare Funds in the prescribed ratio of 50:50, along
with interest @18% per annum from 28 June 2019 till the date of deposit. Further, the Tribunal has imposed a penalty @ 10% of
the profiteered amount with the provision that the penalty shall not be payable if the entire profiteered amount along with
applicable interest is deposited within 30 days from the date of the order. The appeal to the said order is being preferred before
the Competent court of jurisdiction.
A provision amounting to ₹11,629.85 lakh has been recognised during quarter and half year ended 30 September 2026 and
disclosed as an exceptional item in the financial results. The provision includes the alleged profiteered amount of ₹5,041.44 and
interest @18% per annum up to 30 September 2026.

The above consolidated results are based on the management certified financial statements of IRCTC Payments Ltd. (Subsidiary
Company). 
The figures for the previous year/periods have been regrouped/reclassified/restated, wherever considered necessary.
In line with Railway Board Commercial Circular No. CC-60 of 2019 on increase in catering tariff for post-paid and pre-paid trains, the
Company raised demands for enhanced licence fee for the periods 18th November 2019 to 22nd March 2020 (post-paid trains) and
27th November 2021 to 30th September 2026 (post-paid and pre-paid trains). Certain licensees have challenged the demands
before High Courts or invoked arbitration. Awards passed against the Company in some cases have been challenged before the
Hon’ble Delhi High Court, which has stayed their execution; the matter is next listed on 18th January, 2027.
As the matter is sub-judice, the enhanced licence fee for the periods 18th November 2019 to 22nd March 2020 (post-paid trains)
and 27th November 2021 to 30th September 2026 (post-paid and pre-paid trains) has not been recognised in the results for the
quarter and half-year ended 30th September 2026, the corresponding comparative periods and the year ended 31 March 2026,
consistent with earlier periods.
As per the terms and conditions of the tender, in respect of the four PPP Railneer plants, the Developer-cum-Operators (DCOs) are
to be reimbursed the GST on the supply of Railneer, net of the Input Tax Credit (ITC) availed by them. However, complete
information regarding the ITC availed by the DCOs is not available. Based on the information made available by certain DCOs, an
amount of ₹ 99.32 lakhs and ₹ 192.00 lakhs has been accounted for as a claim by the Company towards ITC for the quarter and half
year ended 30 September 2026, respectively, and an amount of ₹ 397.86 lakhs was accounted for during FY 2025-26. Accordingly,
the total amount accounted for in the books of the Company aggregates to ₹ 1847.30 lakhs and ₹ 2039.30 lakhs as at 31 March
2026 and 30 September 2026, respectively. The DCOs have contested the Company's claim towards ITC. 
The management has issued letters to the DCOs directing them to furnish GSTR data, so as to enable IRCTC to ascertain the actual
ITC availed by them. Based on such data, recovery of ITC shall be affected strictly in accordance with the contract conditions.
The DCOs of Sankrail, Hapur & Nagpur plants have challenged the same before the Hon’ble Court. In case of Sankrail Plant, the
Hon’ble Delhi High Court has appointed an Arbitrator and restrained the Company from taking any recovery related steps in respect
of any amount pertaining to the alleged input tax credit until the learned Sole Arbitrator takes up the application under Section 17
for consideration. Similarly, in respect of Hapur and Nagpur plants, the matter are under arbitration before a common Sole
Arbitrator for these DCOs. In case of Parassala Plant, contract has been terminated and a notice of dispute has already been issued.
Necessary action will be taken in accordance with the concession agreement of Parassala Plant.
The National Anti-Profiteering Authority (NAA) had issued a notice dated 25 February, 2022 alleging profiteering of ₹5041.44 lakh
under CGST Act, 2017 for on account of non-passing the benefit of tax reduction to consumers. The show cause notice was
contested by the Company; however, no order was passed by the Authority. Subsequently, Competition Commission of India (CCI)
was empowered to adjudicate the matter. The matter was taken up by the Principal bench of the Hon'ble Goods & Services Tax
Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT).
The Hon'ble GSTAT, vide its judgment dated 14 October 2026, has passed an order against the Company in relation to proceedings
under Section 171 of the CGST Act, 2017, concerning alleged profiteering in respect of Rail Neer packaged drinking water. The
Hon'ble Tribunal has accepted the DGAP report dated 11 June 2021 and directed the Company to deposit the alleged profiteered
amount of ₹5,041.44 lakh in the Central and State Consumer Welfare Funds in the prescribed ratio of 50:50, along with interest
@18% per annum from 28 June 2019 till the date of deposit. Further, the Tribunal has imposed a penalty @ 10% of the profiteered
amount with the provision that the penalty shall not be payable if the entire profiteered amount along with applicable interest is
deposited within 30 days from the date of the order. The appeal to the said order is being preferred before the Competent court of
jurisdiction.
A provision amounting to ₹11,629.85 lakh has been recognised during quarter and half year ended 30 September 2026 and
disclosed as an exceptional item in the financial results. The provision includes the alleged profiteered amount of ₹5,041.44 and
interest @18% per annum up to 30 September 2026.
